businessRequirements.title: A payment token used as Segment 100 Account Number shall be a valid 13-19 digit token value subject to account validation and designated token BIN rules.
Payment Token Expiration Date shall be populated in the PAN Expiration Date field when token processing requires it.
In-App token cryptogram data shall use the source-defined 28-byte or 56-byte base64 representation and token-data-block interpretation.
56 bytes of cryptogram data shall be interpreted as Token Data Block A followed by Token Data Block B; 28 bytes of cryptogram data shall be interpreted as Token Data Block A only.
A payment token value must not be the same value as the cardholder's actual PAN.
A payment token shall pass basic account-number validation rules, including the LUHN check, and shall fall within a BIN range designated and flagged as a token BIN range.
Tokenized Segment 100 transactions shall use a POS Entry Mode that identifies the token presentment mode.
An EMV Segment 100 transaction shall include Segment 130 EMV Request Data in Data Section 3.
EMV Chip Data shall begin with a valid three-digit length consistent with the following encoded chip data.
EMV Chip Data shall preserve valid BCD-packed/hex TLV tag, length, and value structure.
EMV chip values such as authorized amount, transaction type, currency, and terminal country shall agree with the Segment 100 transaction context.
A CA Public Key file shall use the CA_KEYS file name, version, comma-separated records, and CRLF termination.
Each CA Public Key record shall contain valid expiry date, SHA-1 hash indicator, RSA algorithm indicator, RID, index, modulus, exponent, and checksum fields.
An EMV Segment 100/130 transaction shall use CA key configuration consistent with the applicable EMV AID and public-key data.
EMV Additional Information Table ID 001 shall use the source-defined length and EMVYES/EMVNOT request values.
CARC Additional Information Table ID 002 shall carry the one-character Card Authentication Results Code returned by Visa.
EMV Table Data included in an authorization response shall be echoed in subsequent advice or batch-upload requests when required by the source.
A 3-D Secure Authorization Response shall return the applicable ECI/Terminal Type value (25, 26, 27, 28, or 29) together with the card-brand cryptogram: Visa CAVV, MasterCard AAV, or Amex AEVV.

For Visa token-based transactions combined with 3-D Secure, the TAVV token cryptogram and the 3DS CAVV cryptogram (revised format) shall be populated per the defined Verified-by-Visa-only, Digital-Wallet-only, or combined scenario.
Amex SafeKey transactions shall be sent with indicator 'SK' followed by 56 bytes of SafeKey data in base64 format; when the first 28 bytes are not applicable, they shall be space-filled.

MasterCard AAV cryptogram data shall use Segment 111 Table ID 36 (UCAF Data) while Token/DSRP cryptograms shall use Segment 123 Element 237 (TAVV); when both are present, the UCAF Security Level Code shall be '21' (Channel Encrypted).
Segment 100 messages use Appendix A TCP/IP framing rules for message length, byte order, TPDU protocol, and reserved addresses.
Segment 100 Terminal Identifier and conditional state context use valid Appendix D state-code families.
Segment 100 financial Prompt Codes use valid Appendix E card types and separate special Prompt Code families.
Segment 100 fuel/product transactions use Appendix F Product Codes through Segment 102 and reconcile product totals to Segment 100 amounts.
Segment 100 Prompt Code transaction type uses the applicable Appendix G financial or special transaction family.
Segment 100 financial responses interpret Appendix H decline codes for re-entry, timeout, retry, recurring-payment, and token behavior.
Conditional Segment 111 Variable Information uses the applicable Appendix I Table ID and layout.
POS Entry Mode in Segment 111 uses Appendix J PAN and terminal capability values and persists through lifecycle exceptions.
Segment 100 financial responses use Appendix K Additional Information Table IDs and layouts when Element 116 indicates additional data.
Currency values in Segment 100-related transaction and variable data use valid Appendix L currency codes.
EBT/eWIC Segment 103 Element 164 uses Appendix M total length, tagged subelements, and program-data formats.
Tokenized Segment 100 transactions use Appendix O token account, expiration, cryptogram, and presentment concepts where applicable.
Segment 111 Table 030 POS Condition Code uses Appendix Q terminal, presentation, security, and terminal-type values.
EMV Segment 100 transactions include Segment 130 and validate Appendix R chip-data framing and context consistency.
EMV Additional Information associated with Segment 100/130 uses Appendix T Table IDs and response echo behavior.
A standard non-EMV request may contain Segment 100 only when no additional data is required.
An EMV purchase must include Segment 130 with Segment 100.
A fleet transaction requiring fleet data must include Segment 101 with Segment 100.
A fuel transaction requiring product data must include Segment 102 with Segment 100.
A transaction with multiple applicable data categories must include Segment 100 and every required companion segment.
An unknown segment combination must be held for review rather than silently accepted or rejected.
eWIC Authorization/Benefits Inquiry uses Prompt Code 3086 and Segment 103.
eWIC Authorization Cancellation uses Prompt Code S086 and Segment 103.
eWIC Balance Inquiry uses Prompt Code E086 and Segment 103.
eWIC Purchase Completion uses Prompt Code 0086, Segment 103, and original lifecycle identity.
eWIC Voucher Clear uses Prompt Code 0086 and applicable Segment 103 voucher data.
eWIC Purchase Reversal/Void uses Prompt Code 8086 and completes before another eWIC transaction.
eWIC Segment 103 carries valid WIC discount, product, and EBT program data within source-defined lengths.
Segment 100 Information Byte shall use the source-defined single-message, multimessage, or download value.
Segment 100 shall contain the account number or identification value required by the transaction context.
Card Discretionary Block Data shall be validated to its source-defined conditional length and usage.
Encrypted PIN Block Data shall use the source-defined DUKPT KSN and PIN-block representation when PIN processing applies.
Pump/Lane Number shall be present and correctly formatted when the transaction is a fuel or lane-specific flow.
Fuel Purchase Amount shall represent the net fuel amount when fuel purchase data applies.
Nonfuel Amount shall represent the net nonfuel, noncash, and nontax amount when applicable.
Tax Amount shall represent the total tax amount when tax data applies.
Cash Amount shall represent the total cash amount when cash data applies.
Approval Number shall be validated when the transaction flow requires an approval reference.
Local Date and Local Time shall use the source-defined ten-character representation when required by the flow.
An EBT flow requiring EBT data shall include Segment 103 in addition to Segment 100.
A purchase-card flow requiring purchase-card data shall include Segment 104 in addition to Segment 100.
A flow requiring variable information shall include Segment 111 in addition to Segment 100.
An NFC tokenized flow shall include Segment 123 in addition to Segment 100.
A Moneris authorizer flow shall include Segment 135 in addition to Segment 100.
TCP/IP Message Length equals the bytes following the length field.
TCP/IP Message Length uses network byte order.
TPDU Protocol ID must be 0x60.
Reserved TPDU destination and source addresses must be zero when sending to BUYPASS.
Element 55 Message Format Version Identifier must be ATL105.
Element 63 must equal the number of serialized segments.
Data Section 1 separators must surround Element 63 correctly.
Segment Type must be 100 for the Standard Message Data Segment.
Segment Length must represent encoded Segment 100 content.
Terminal Identifier is 1-22 alphanumeric characters for a financial flow.
Terminal Identifier is at most 13 characters for load flows.
Composite Terminal Identifier matches device, state, merchant, and device-number components when those components are modeled.
Prompt Code first position identifies a supported transaction type.
Prompt Code remaining positions identify the expected card type or flow code.
Account Number representation must agree with the declared POS entry method.
Tokenized or TransArmor account representation must be explicit.
Sequence Number must be six digits.
Completion, reversal, void, and timeout flows must reuse the original Sequence Number.
Partial Approval Indicator must use an allowed value.
Partial Approval Indicator value 5 requires Amex prepaid balance-receipt context.
Empty non-trailing Segment 100 fields retain separators.
Unneeded trailing optional Segment 100 fields are omitted.
Lifecycle follow-up messages reuse original sequence and approval references.
Authorization completion reuses the original Sequence Number.
Authorization void reuses the original Sequence Number.
Refund void of return reuses the original Sequence Number.
Sale void reuses the original Sequence Number.
A timeout reversal reuses the Sequence Number of the timed-out request.
An EMV request without Segment 130 is invalid.
A fleet request without required Segment 101 is invalid.
A fuel request without required Segment 102 is invalid.
Element 63 must equal the actual number of serialized segments.
A companion segment must not be duplicated unless the specification explicitly allows repetition.
Segments must follow the applicable ATL105 serialization order.
An unmapped segment combination requires review.
Segment 100 purchase responses support approved purchase/capture outcomes.
Segment 100 authorization responses support approved authorization outcomes.
Segment 100 supports partial approval with an approved amount.
Segment 100 declined responses carry a decline code.
Fleet Data Segment is a Data Section 3 companion of Segment 100.
Fleet Data Segment is required in every fleet-card financial transaction request.
Fleet Data Segment must not coexist with Enhanced Fleet Data Segment (145).
Segment Type is 101.
Segment Length is 3 digits representing the content length.
Base Segment 101 max length is 61 alphanumeric characters.
Field order matches Section 12.2 (base fields 1-13, tag fields 14-18).
Odometer is numeric max 8 digits when populated.
User ID is alphanumeric max 12 and non-zero when populated.
Fleet Tag fields appear only in Auth Completion (0220) messages.
Fleet Tag code must be one of the 17 valid codes.
Fleet Tag payload conforms to per-code format.
At most one Segment 101 per message.
EBT Data Segment is a Data Section 3 companion segment usable in any field slot.
Segment Type is 103.
Segment Length is 3 or 4 digits; 4 digits required for EBT-with-eWIC transactions.
Segment 103 maximum length is 3,334 alphanumeric characters.
Clerk ID is numeric max 10 when populated.
Voucher ID is numeric max 10 when populated.
WIC Discount Amount uses the positional Account Type/Amount Type/Currency Code/signed Amount format.
WIC Product Data begins with a 4-digit Total Length subelement bounded to 2997.
EBT Program Data begins with a 3-digit Total Length subelement bounded to 264.
EBT Program Data subelement TAG must be one of the documented values.
EBT Program Data subelement with TAG 50 requires ACCOUNT TYPE 98.
At most one Segment 103 per message.
Segment Type field in the Purchase Card Data Segment has fixed value 104.
Segment Length identifies the Purchase Card Data Segment's total length including Segment Type and Field Separators.
The Purchase Card Data Segment has a maximum length of 86 alphanumeric characters.
Segment 108 is exclusive to the Loyalty Card Transaction Request.
Segment Type is 108.
Segment Length is 3 digits.
Segment 108 maximum length is 142 alphanumeric characters.
Loyalty Program ID is required, numeric max 6.
Loyalty Account Number is numeric max 24 when populated.
Update Code, when populated, is one of the documented values.
Payment Tender Type is required and one of the documented values.
At most one Segment 108 per message.
Segment Type field in the Variable Information Data Segment has fixed value 111.
Segment Length identifies the Variable Information Data Segment's total length including Segment Type and Field Separators.
The Variable Information Data Segment has a maximum length of 999 alphanumeric characters.
Field Separators do not appear between elements within a Variable Information Section repetition or between repetitions; a single Field Separator follows the final repetition.
Segment 113 is exclusive to the ECA/TeleCheck Service Transaction Request.
Segment Type is 113.
Segment Length is 3 digits.
Segment 113 maximum length is 156 alphanumeric characters.
ECA/TeleCheck Clerk ID is required, alphanumeric max 6.
ECA/TeleCheck Trace ID, when populated, is alphanumeric max 22; required on Void requests.
Segment 113 appears at most once per message.

testCases.positive: Valid tokenized account representation that is not the actual PAN and passes LUHN
Token expiration, cryptogram block split, and entry mode agree with token context
negative: 56-byte cryptogram not split into Block A/B

testCases.positive: EMV tags agree with Segment 100 context
Valid CA_KEYS file and CA public-key record
EMV AID resolves to valid configured CA key
EMVYES or EMVNOT uses Table ID 001
CARC uses Table ID 002 and one-character result
Response EMV data is preserved into required follow-up message
Valid ECI value with matching brand cryptogram
negative: ECI value outside 25-29 for a 3DS transaction

testCases.positive: TAVV/CAVV combination matches the declared scenario
negative: TAVV present without applicable token context
missing space-fill on inapplicable first 28 bytes

testCases.positive: AAV in Table ID 36, TAVV/DSRP in Segment 123, Security Level Code '21' when both present
negative: AAV and DSRP cryptogram fields swapped
missing Security Level Code '21' when both present

testData.reason: Token length/BIN/Luhn format validation can use synthetic token values; does not require a live token vault.
Token-vs-PAN equality check is a simple synthetic comparison.
LUHN check and BIN-range membership are algorithmic and synthesizable.
Field-population format check only.
Validates 28/56-byte base64 length and token-data-block framing only, not cryptographic authenticity.
Block A/B length split is a structural byte-offset check, not cryptographic verification.
POS Entry Mode context check only.
Segment 130 presence and Element 63 count are structural checks; synthetic placeholder chip data is sufficient.
Length-prefix validation is structural; does not require a genuine EMV card/kernel.
BCD/hex TLV tag-length-value framing is structural and synthesizable.
Amount/currency/transaction-type cross-check compares plaintext TLV values against Segment 100 fields; no cryptographic verification involved.

No current BR claims cryptographic verification of the 9F26 Application Cryptogram (ARQC/TC); genuine verification requires a certified EMV kernel or HSM and cannot be synthesized. Tracked here so this boundary is explicit if such a BR is added later.
File name, version, delimiter, and CRLF termination are structural checks on a synthetic CA_KEYS file.
Record layout and checksum algorithm can be validated against a self-consistent synthetic key record; does not require a genuine production RSA key.
Confirming that a real EMV AID resolves to the correct production CA key requires the actual First Data/network-issued key file; a synthetic key cannot validate genuine AID-to-key resolution.
EMVYES/EMVNOT is a fixed enumerated value; fully synthesizable.
CARC is a one-character format check; the value itself is a network-returned result, not cryptographic material.
Echo-preservation is a byte-for-byte carryover check across messages; synthetic EMV Table Data is sufficient.
ECI value and cryptogram byte-length/format can be validated with synthetic placeholders; does not verify cryptographic authenticity.
Validating the TAVV/CAVV scenario matrix against a real transaction requires genuine Visa-issued token/3DS cryptograms; a synthetic pairing cannot confirm scenario correctness.
56-byte base64 format and space-fill rule are structural checks; synthetic SafeKey data is sufficient.
Verifying genuine AAV/DSRP cryptogram placement and correctness requires real MasterCard SecureCode/DSRP-issued data; a synthetic value cannot confirm cryptographic correctness.
